'''Tomasz''' "'''Tomek'''" '''Bartoszyński''' (born 16 May 1957) is a [[Poland|Polish]]<!-- is that right? -->-American mathematician who works in [[set theory]]. 

==Biography==
Bartoszyński studied mathematics at the [[University of Warsaw]] from 1976 to 1981, and worked there from 1981 to 1987.   In 1984, he defended his Ph.D. thesis ''Combinatorial aspects of measure and category''; his advisor was Wojciech Guzicki.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=74715}}</ref> In 2004, he received his [[habilitation]] from the [[Polish Academy of Sciences]].

From 1986 onward, he worked in the United States: he taught at the [[University of California|University of California, Berkeley]] and [[University of California, Davis]]. From 1990 to 2006, he was a professor (full professor from 1998-2006) at [[Boise State University]].

In 1990-1991, he visited the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]] as a [[Lady Davis Fellows|fellow of the Lady Davis foundation]], and in 1996/97 he visited the [[Free University of Berlin]] as a [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation|Humboldt fellow]]. Currently, {{when|date=April 2024}} he is one of the program directors at the [[National Science Foundation]] (NSF), responsible for [[combinatorics]], [[foundations of mathematics|foundations]], and [[probability]].

== Family ==
His father, Robert Bartoszyński, is a statistician. 

His wife, Joanna Kania-Bartoszyńska, is the NSF program director for [[topology]] and [[geometric analysis]].

== Scientific work==
Bartoszyński's work is mainly concerned with [[forcing (set theory)|forcing]], specifically with applications of forcing to the [[set theory of the real line]].   He has written about 50 papers in this field, as well as a monograph: 
* Tomek Bartoszyński and  [[Haim Judah]]: ''Set theory. On the structure of the real line.'' A K Peters, Ltd., Wellesley, MA, 1995; {{ISBN|1-56881-044-X}}
